name: `t Goeie Doelen Winkeltje
description_short: At 't Goeie Doelen Winkeltje you can buy second-hand items for a reasonable price. There is furniture, lamps, books, DVDs, clothing, toys, crockery and much more. Then you have come to the right place at Dock van Delft! This beautiful meeting center, located in the heart of Delft, offers a warm and hospitable environment where everyone feels welcome. Dock van Delft is there for people who need more support than a community center or association can offer, but who still want to be at the center of life. With us you can participate in various activities in a relaxed manner, enjoy delicious meals and, above all, have fun with others. Whether you like creative workshops, games, music or just a good conversation – there is something for everyone! Senior citizen's center Residents of surrounding neighborhoods and residents of Ezelsveldlaan are welcome in the senior center on Tuesday mornings. Talk together and drink a cup of coffee or tea. Sharing interests and perhaps friendships...

name: Abstract schilderen vanaf 18 jaar
description_short: You learn to look at the subject 'meaninglessly' and to translate it into line, plane, composition and shades of light and color.
description_full: Abstract painting from the age of 18 Back to the overview Abstract: difficult or easy? No, just fun! This course starts with an introduction and then goes into more detail about the 'building blocks' for an abstract painting. The abstract course suits everyone, both beginners and advanced. The same principles apply to an abstract work of art as to a realistic work of art. In fact, to create a realistic work one must learn to look 'abstractly'. One must look at the subject 'meaninglessly' and translate it into line, plane, composition and shades of light and color. In the Abstract Painting course we take these basic principles as a starting point to create an abstract work. We initially do this with a number of exercises in which these principles are discussed. We then work on assignments where these are used in combination using examples of well-known and lesser-known artists. The course is therefore also a journey of discovery through art history. The pleasure of making is paramount in the course. You can join at any level. The teacher tries to adapt the lesson program as much as possible to the personal wishes of the students. For example, if the group wishes to delve deeper into a particular artist, Machiel is happy to include that in the lesson. Register Teachers Machiel van Soest About the lessons Each student receives access to the course website where each lesson is supported with images and reading material and where all lessons can be viewed. The lesson starts with a presentation in which the theme is explained using many examples. For inspiration and to help you explore new paths. There is plenty of room for personal input, development and experiment. At the end of the lesson we have a group discussion of the work. It is possible to participate in a group exhibition in OPEN and thus show your works of art to a wider audience and to your friends and family. Once a year we take an excursion to an exhibition. View an example lesson. What should I bring? All general painting materials and tools are provided, plus storage space for your workpieces. The material costs are not included in the course price. For this course you pay € 90.00 in material costs. You pay these costs to the teacher during the first lesson. Teaching method Abstract painting is a group course. The number of participants is a maximum of 15. name: After Nature vanaf 18 jaar
description_short: In this course we draw and paint animal studies based on observations of various natural history specimens in the room.
description_full: After Nature from 18 years Back to the overview Realistic drawing and painting from nature How do you draw or paint a talking animal head? Sparkling plumage or beautiful insect wings? The special thing about this drawing and painting course is that we make animal studies based on observation using a collection of real natural history specimens that are set up in the classroom. While studying the various objects, you discuss with the teacher what you experience as aesthetic about the animal or what repels you. Your interpretation in the representation of the animal is important and through various studies you will learn to depict the various special characteristics of the animal. In principle we work from perception in a figurative style, but there is room for interpretation and abstraction. Register Teachers Gurt Swanenberg What will you learn during this course? First of all, it is the sense of wonder that counts. An animal specimen gives you the opportunity to study it endlessly and experience its beauty. Every little detail, beautiful plumage, pattern in a coat or a scaly tail can be a revelation and invite you to study. You learn to build up a painting from a sketch, using various materials, such as chalk/charcoal, ink, acrylic and watercolor paint. During the lessons we look at many natural history studies by artists from the past. The aim is to gain insight into how natural science has served as inspiration for the arts over the centuries. We look at which features of the animal the artist has highlighted, and how he dealt with composition, shape and color. In 18 lessons we create a mini-portfolio in which you display various animal studies in various materials. What should I bring? You don't need to bring anything. The teacher provides all drawing and painting materials and paper/canvas. Useful to know The course price does not include €42.50 in material costs. description_full: Creative drawing & painting 10 to 15 years Back to the overview Discover and develop your own drawing style This drawing technique course of 3×11 lessons is for participants who want to further develop their drawing skills. We use various materials such as ink, markers, chalk and conté charcoal. You will gain more insight into modern and classical drawing techniques. And we also make trips to painting. This drawing technique course is for students who already have more experience with drawing and want to develop their drawing techniques and creative ideas even further. Register Teachers Marieke Thiescheffer Learn drawing techniques and develop your own drawing style. In class we use various materials such as ink, markers, chalk, conté and charcoal. If you want, you can also paint with watercolor paint or acrylic paint. You will learn to apply the following technical concepts: composition, line, tonality, shape and volume, looking, portrait (eyes, nose and mouth), model, perspective, illustration. Attention is paid to concepts such as abstraction, dots and surfaces, drawing (natural) materials and collage technique. The lessons pay special attention to the development of your personal style. The course is for teenagers who already have experience with drawing. Drawing is the basis for, for example, architecture, the arts, illustration and design (from cities, fashion to design). Even if you only work with computer programs later. There are often examples from drawing that can inspire you to do a technical assignment. Think of Tje Tjong Khing, Andy Warhol, Michelangelo, Schoonhoven, Klee, Mondriaan, Escher. And also lesser-known artists who have made appealing drawings. About the lessons The first half hour of each lesson focuses on the discovery of a new material or technique. This is done together, after which you continue working on your own drawing individually. What should I bring? All materials are already present! description_full: Creative toddler course 2 to 4 years Back to the overview Discover, play and create together with your toddler — in a quiet, pleasant setting where fun, creativity and development come together. This course is about taking time, being curious and exploring the world together through various techniques, materials and color. By creating together, trust and closeness grow. It is precisely these kinds of little moments that linger and that deepen the bond between parent and child in a gentle way. For toddlers, creative work is a very natural way to learn. By feeling, moving and experimenting they develop their motor skills, concentration and self-confidence. At the same time, fantasy and free thinking are given plenty of space. Because this play largely takes place before language, it is a perfect fit for young children — without explanation, without having to. Register Teachers Nancy Tjong develop through play. Being creative supports the sensory and motor development of young children. Spending time together Really working together strengthens the bond between parent and child. Small-scale and quiet Small groups provide overview, attention and a pleasant atmosphere. A creative basis Getting to know materials and shapes in a playful way stimulates creative thinking. Fun is central. There is no pressure to perform; discovery and enjoyment are paramount. What can you expect? The course consists of five lessons of 60 minutes. Parent and child work together with different materials, always at the pace and based on the child's curiosity. Everything is ready — all you have to do is come and join in. A nice moment together In the hustle and bustle of everyday life, these moments are rare. This course offers a quiet, creative moment to work together. Good to know: Wear clothes that you don't mind getting dirty. name: Illustratie / Beeldcultuur vanaf 18 jaar
description_short: In this course we look at the function of the image in illustration and art and at the origins of the image.
description_full: Illustration / Visual culture from the age of 18 Back to the overview Will AI soon dominate visual culture? Perhaps, but then the authenticity, the place of the image in tradition or ritual, also disappears. In this course we look at the function of the image in illustration and art and at the origins of the image. You are offered nine very different themes that you work on for a month. During each first lesson of the month, the teacher provides an introduction to the theme that will be covered that month. The introduction consists of background information regarding the role of illustration within the theme. Because you talk to your teacher about your thoughts on the theme, you get a personal view on the interpretation of the illustrations to be made. Because you work on various assignments within the theme for a month, you gain insight into how you can best represent it. Ultimately, you present your illustrations/ideas in the last lesson of the month, explaining to the other students what choices you have made to represent the theme as best as possible, and which elements in the theme are important to you. Because you can talk about your own work with your teacher and other students as a sounding board, you learn a lot about how others see your work and whether what you wanted to say has been presented correctly. Register Teachers Gurt Swanenberg Although an illustration normally only has a supplementary function to a text and does not in principle stand on its own, in some themes you are encouraged to make an autonomous drawing or painting that can stand on its own. (That is why we always look at how the theme offered is depicted in the visual arts.) The themes always include technical exercises to continue developing your drawing and painting technique. What could such a theme look like? An example of such a theme that was worked on in the 2024/2025 season: Subject/theme: the role of illustration surrounding propaganda during the colonization of Africa. Introduction of the function of illustrations in Western European newspapers to justify military expeditions in African countries (1800/1900). And thus putting the indigenous population in a bad light. With practical drawing assignment about political propaganda. Nostalgia and cliché; the photography of Jimmy Nelson. (Photography of indigenous tribes). With practical drawing assignment/collage exercise about different external characteristics of indigenous tribes. What should I bring? Various drawing/painting materials, paper and brushes are available. Material costs are not included in the course price. For this course you pay €80 in material costs. You pay these costs to the teacher during the first lesson. description_full: Ceramics - free sculpting from 18 years old Back to the overview For everyone with a passion for sculpture, clay and ceramics In the course you will make sculptures with clay. Ceramics is a discipline with an enormous variety of possibilities. Ceramics is a real voyage of discovery. The more experience you gain, the more is possible. You develop your own style. Step by step you will learn the process of making ceramic sculptures. In the ceramics city of Delft, with a centuries-old tradition of making ceramics, the profession is still alive and kicking. Ceramics is a popular discipline in contemporary art, and many young artists have rediscovered the ceramic technique. The Ceramics - Free Modeling course is intended for students aged 18 and over, with or without experience. Register Teachers Pepijn van den Nieuwendijk What will you learn during the free modeling course? During the course you will work independently. Based on your own idea or sketch design. Figurative or abstract. Pepijn van den Nieuwendijk guides you through the process of making a ceramic sculpture. The image can be constructed in different ways. You learn to build a hollow or solid statue, after which the statue must then be hollowed out. You will learn step by step the different stages of the ceramic process. Everyone can work at their own level in this ceramics course - from beginner to advanced. When the statue is ready, it is dried and baked. You will then glaze and decorate the work, after which it will be fired again. During the course you will learn about the wide possibilities in the design of ceramics and the great diversity in glaze decoration techniques. description_full: Art lessons 10 to 15 years Back to the overview The aim of this course is to set the child free and undertake a search for his own style. The child thereby broadens his own possibilities. Every year, the art lessons for children course consists of three blocks with its own theme. We use that theme as a basis for research. We inspire, stimulate the imagination and take a journey through artists and techniques. We draw and paint, but we also build, take photographs or make an animation video. The aim of this course is to set the child free and embark on a search for his or her own style. The child thereby broadens his own possibilities. Register Teachers Carine Hooykaas Hilke Zoontjens Carine Hooykaas Protest Art 13-9-2025 to 29-11-2025 In this block we jump on the barricade and make works that are for or against something. We look at artists who give their opinion very clearly and visibly, such as Bansky and Wim T. Schippers. What protest is hidden in the work of Frida Kahlo and Da Vinci. We work in a wide variety of techniques, such as stickers, stencil printing and paintings. Bizarre 13-12-2025 to 14-3-2026 In the Bizarre block we delve into the world of Hieronymus Bosch and Victor Brauner and others. We make works about people, animals and buildings that make no sense. We look for the monsters that live in our bad dreams and create the most bizarre works of them. A fantastically scary block. Color… doesn't clash. 28-3-2026 to 4-7-2026 The block is about shape and color and the wonders of mixing paint, pencil and chalk. How does that work and why does yellow and blue become green? Mixing colors is like arithmetic, 1 + 1 = 3. The works we are going to make are somewhere between abstract and figurative. We look at the work of Franz Marc, Albers and Delaunay, among others. description_short: What you cut away becomes white; what remains, you print. This is how you build up an image layer by layer. Learn to develop your own visual language.
description_full: Lino & woodcut, graphic studio in-depth from 18 years Back to the overview During this in-depth course you will be introduced to a printing technique that works like a stamp. What you cut away becomes white; what remains, you print. This is how you build up an image layer by layer. By repeating, shifting or combining, new variations are always created. In this course you will explore the many possibilities of the lino and woodcut technique. You will learn different ways to print with color. For example, with Chine-collé, which is a refined printing technique in which a thin sheet of paper is glued to a sturdier background sheet during printing. There is also room for experiment. Consider blind printing, where you do not use ink but create a relief, or printing on different supports such as textiles and wallpaper. Is there interest in the group? Then we investigate together what else is possible. You will discover how contemporary artists use this technique – and what you can use it for. You don't need to have any experience. In this course you will learn to master the technique and develop your own visual language. description_full: Masterclass Carla Klein from 16 years Back to the overview Painting with a photo as a starting point During our masterclasses we delve deeper into techniques by providing an insight into the work and working methods of artists. In this Masterclass, Carla Klein takes you into her studio. She explains how her work is constructed, what choices she makes and what is important to her in the artwork. Carla uses photos as a starting point for her canvases. Where not only the image, but also the print itself forms the basis of the final work. In this masterclass, a photo you bring with you is the starting point for your new work of art. Together with Carla you will look and discover what your eye-catcher is and how you will incorporate it into your painted work. Do you dare to deviate from your path with an open mind? "Making a painting is a sum of moments, ideas, energy, mood and looking. It may well be that the final painting is not at all what you expected or what you wanted. Sometimes it is good to let a painting grow 'on its own' and move along with the wonderful possibilities that creating an image entails and ultimately be surprised by your own painting. The best thing is when a painting goes in a different direction but ultimately is exactly what you initially wanted." Register Teachers Carla Klein The lessons explained Step 1 Bring a photo, printed or original. Also take some extra copies with you. Choose a photo that makes you feel, see or think something 'extra'. It could be anything, a childhood photo, a memory, a failed photo (which does not show exactly what it was about) or the perfect photo of which you would prefer to make a painting. Find out why you chose this photo and try to put it into words and visually isolate it from the rest of the photo. Then we will first make a number of studies: You paint a number of things 'away' on the prints and you try capture the main objective You emphasize what is important in the photo by outlining, coloring or giving attention in another way. Change the frame. Make it elongated, smaller, only a detail, this makes the image stronger. Step 3 Complete the image by, for example: Keeping the background light to be completely removed. To paint only the essential elements/lines of the background. Something you come up with yourself: you can think about color, brush stroke, thickness of paint. To add another image that reinforces the main goal. Now you have a number of different image options or sketches for your final work of art. Step 4 We look at which option works best for your main goal. And also whether something has emerged that appeals to you much more. Dare to deviate from your path by looking carefully with an open mind, other students can help you with this. Step 5 It is now time to make a real painting! We choose a sketch that appeals to you the most. Creating a painting is a sum of moments, ideas, mood and viewing or what you wanted. Sometimes it is good to let a painting grow 'on its own' and move along with the wonderful possibilities that creating an image brings and ultimately be surprised by...

description_full: Masterclass Gurt Swanenberg from 16 years Back to the overview Natural history illustration Natural history illustration is primarily an art form that aims to accurately depict plants, animals and other aspects of nature. It continues to be used in scientific research, education and conservation efforts. Of course, photography and other advanced technology have partially eliminated the need for illustration when studying new species. However, the illustrator can bring life and detail to a subject by adding color/texture that might be missing in photography alone. The workshop is a fun mix of science and creativity. We look at the different aspects of art and nature in five themes: Register Teachers Gurt Swanenberg 1: History of exploration: Illustrations of exotic plants and animals from the colonies. The focus is mainly on two special artists and naturalists: Maria Sybille Merian (1647-1717), with plant and insect studies made in Suriname, and Berthe Hoola van Nooten (1817-1892), who illustrated the flora of Java. In this lesson there is a brief introduction to the two above-mentioned artists and their working method is discussed. Then there is a brief introduction to the watercolor method. An insect or plant study is then made in watercolor based on the existing collection. 2: The “Sottobosco”, The still life of the forest floor. Never before have runts had their own art genre. A fascinating, dark world of fallen and rotting tree stumps, mushrooms, mosses and the slithering and hissing of snakes, lizards and toads. Two artists who, among other things, were concerned with this theme are presented: Melchior d'Hondecoeter (1636-1695) and Otto Marseus van Schrieck (1613-1678). In this lesson there is a brief introduction to the two above-mentioned artists and their working methods are discussed. Then there is a brief introduction to the working method with acrylic. Then a small study of a forest floor is made, as the two artists mentioned also did, by pressing real moss and plants into the wet layer of paint to imitate the structure of the forest floor. 3: Discovery of the microscope: based on the studies of Ernst Haeckel (1834-1919), in this lesson we mainly talk about the layout of your page and composition. In this workshop we look at the shapes of microscopic creatures, both plants and animals. In this lesson there is a brief introduction to the above-mentioned zoologist and philosopher. We then use watercolor to make a number of studies on paper that already has a color, we mainly look at the representation of transparent creatures such as single-celled organisms, jellyfish, etc... 4: Based on the bird studies of John James Audubon (1785-1851), we make this lesson on bird studies, based on the available collection of stuffed birds. Once again, the composition is particularly important, but extra attention is also paid to the fabric expression of the plumage. In this lesson you can experiment with chalk, but also make a study of your bird in acrylic. We also look at Audubon's choices, in particular his way of making a composite.5: Presenting a collection/the “Wunderkammer” collection and natural history illustration in applied art. In this lesson we look at the collected work of Albertus Seba (1665-1736), the insect designs of Eugène Alain Séguy (1890-1985) and the nostalgia for “wild nature” and the chamber of wonders. With a special role for the work of Douanier Rousseau. The lesson starts with an introduction to the above-mentioned artists. In this lesson we look at how you can reuse the different studies for designs, as patterns for clothing design, for example. Attention is also paid to the renewed interest in wild nature. 6: The sixth and final lesson is to collect all the work and finish...

name: Masterclass Machiel van Soest vanaf 16 jaar
description_short: In this masterclass we discuss the techniques of the old masters. We will make a painting together, step by step.
description_full: Masterclass Machiel van Soest from 16 years Back to the overview Masterclass Grisaille by teacher and artist Machiel van Soest Technique of the old masters In this masterclass we discuss the technique of the old masters. We will make a painting together, step by step. Although this technique seems complicated, it actually makes the painting process easier because you systematically solve the problems you encounter while painting: the drawing, light/dark and color. The core of this classic method consists of treating these three image aspects separately. By following these steps separately, the complexity of the painting process becomes manageable and you increase the chance of a successful result. Since Van Gogh, painting has mainly been done wet-on-wet, which means that painters have to deal with these three aspects at the same time. Although this has resulted in many good and beautiful paintings, it remains difficult for the human brain to simultaneously separate these three aspects while painting. For example, it is very difficult to simultaneously estimate the tonal value of a color and ensure that the brush stroke follows the drawing. This wet-on-wet technique has made paintings simpler and flatter. The old masters strictly adhered to this structured method. That is why you see so many impressive paintings from that period in museums worldwide. They treated the three aspects—drawing, light/dark and color—separately and one after the other, thus maintaining an overview. Once you master this technique, you can paint whatever you want. You can create more complicated paintings and the subject takes on more importance. The firmly structured structure gives you complete freedom to paint whatever comes to mind. You control the paint, not the other way around. Register Teachers Machiel van Soest In this course you will learn: • transfer the drawing to the canvas; • put on the grisaille; • complete the painting with colored transparent layers. What should I bring? All general painting materials and tools are provided, plus storage space for your workpieces. The material costs are not included in the course price. For this course you pay € 15.00 in material costs. You pay these costs to the teacher during the first lesson. description_full: Portrait and model painting from 16 years Back to the overview Painting from a living model In this painting course on Monday afternoons you will work alternately in a short series of portrait painting lessons and a short series of model painting lessons. Jan Wisse's portrait and model painting lessons always involve live models. “Learning to portray is unlearning to paint what you think and paint what you see.” Both beginners and advanced students can make great strides in painting and drawing a portrait or a model in this course. Everyone works at his or her own level. The most important thing is that you enjoy doing it, the rest will follow naturally from the teacher's instructions. This will continually encourage you to improve your qualities. Usually we work on one painting for 3 consecutive afternoons, but there are also short sessions of one afternoon. The sessions start with a short introduction for the entire group. Afterwards, everyone is guided individually. Each afternoon ends together with a discussion of the papers by the teacher in consultation with the students. Register Teachers Jan Wisse What do you learn while painting portraits and models? You will learn to draw and paint the entire human figure and to depict the face as a portrait. You will gradually develop your skills until you can create a similar portrait. You start by learning to draw the correct proportions and then sketch while painting. Then you learn to master spatial imagination and similarity. You will improve your painting technique through the various assignments you receive, such as focusing on shape, color or style. You gradually discover your own style of painting and you are encouraged to do so. What are you bringing? You don't have to lug around stuff, because the course includes the use of all materials and tools. There is also storage space for your workpieces. The painting studio in which we work with the group is professionally equipped. description_full: Portrait and styles from 18 years old Back to the overview The portrait throughout history Portraits are about capturing a person within a moment in time. How we look at portraits and what they tell has changed quite drastically throughout history. We investigate style forms and develop our own style. For anyone who wants more than just painting a head and has experience with drawing and painting. Portrait art has undergone a fascinating evolution over the centuries. From the stately portraits of old masters to the modern interpretations of contemporary artists, the genre continues to fascinate and surprise. During this course I will take you on a journey through the history of portrait art and discover how it has developed into what it is today. description_full: Ratio and Romanticism from 18 years Back to the overview The 18th century saw a range of developments – from the frivolous Rococo to strict neoclassicism, from the thinking of the Enlightenment to the sensibilities of Romanticism. name: Realisme vanaf 18 jaar
description_short: A course dedicated to the love of figurative drawing and painting. Students work on their own portfolio of various object studies in different materials.
description_full: Realism from 18 years Back to the overview A course dedicated to the love of figurative drawing and painting. Students work on a small portfolio of various object studies in different materials. The lessons discuss the diversity of the still life and take a closer look at themes such as the showpiece still life, the vanitas, or the trompe l'oeil. Students mainly work on objects that are present in the room and use them to put together compositions. Various visual aspects are discussed, but the emphasis in this course is on composition and learning to portray material expressions. The challenge lies in trying to visualize various surfaces, glossy, matt, rough or smooth, etc. Various visual aspects are treated to increase the illusion of spaciousness on the flat surface, such as cut-off, overlap and repoussoir. Observe, learn to look carefully and then translate into two dimensions. The pleasure in creating a self-conceived composition is paramount. description_short: Anyone who enjoys it can paint a portrait. First the large shapes, the details will come later.
description_full: Painting from a live model from the age of 16 Back to the overview You can learn portrait painting! In the past, the portrait was regarded as one of the most difficult and highly valued genres in painting. The art and craft of portraiture still fascinates many (amateur) painters all over the world. Fortunately, painting a portrait is less difficult than it seems at first glance: if you look attentively and pay attention to the different aspects of a portrait step by step, a beautiful result will soon come close. Everyone can paint portraits. Anyone with an interest and curiosity about portraits is welcome. In the lessons, everyone is guided at their own level. Starters learn the basics of portrait painting and advanced students learn the tricks of the trade. In the portrait course we work from observation, so always from a live model. Every three lessons and sometimes more often there is a different model. Register Teachers Casper Verborg Learn to look and follow your hand. Everyone gets to work with the materials available. Sometimes there is a specific starting point, such as the technique of a well-known artist or a specific color combination, so that you gradually learn to understand the material and techniques better as the course progresses. The lessons always work with a model. In principle, a model is there for three consecutive lessons, so that there is sufficient time to paint a similar and layered portrait. With a lot of practice you will discover the special features of each face, gain insight into the anatomy and develop your own handwriting. At the end of each lesson, the progress of the portraits is discussed with the entire group. Useful to know The portrait painting course does not include the costs for materials and models. name: Tekenen & schilderen – basis vanaf 16 jaar
description_short: Have you always wondered what it's like to be able to draw or paint? Take the step. Start with the basics.
description_full: Drawing & painting – basics from 16 years Back to the overview A cheerful and challenging journey of discovery through the wonderful world of basic drawing and painting techniques Have you always wondered what it's like to be able to draw or paint? This basic course is for anyone over the age of 16 who wants to get started and wants to discover or rediscover the basic principles of drawing and painting. In practice we have different age groups mixed together. Roughly from 20's to around 70's. This makes it more interesting and, importantly, more enjoyable. Register Teachers Victor Roerade Gurt Swanenberg What do you learn? What are the basics of painting and drawing? Learning to look consciously, converting looking into doing. Technique: How do you paint/draw what you see believably on paper? How to create a believable representation of a 3-d object on a 2-d plane. In other words, suggesting/depicting volume. Key elements of this course: 'Looking' and 'seeing'. Practicing: Form, (and developing a sense of form) Composition Material Color and tone Technique, drawing and painting. (strengthen your own handwriting). Every lesson you practice converting unconscious 'looking' into conscious 'seeing'. For example: How does light fall on a leaf in the sun, what exactly is the shape of the shadow on that same leaf? Or 1 small object, for example painting an apple on a flat surface, that is where the entire art of painting lies. You practice certain basic drawing and/or painting techniques through specific assignments, step by step. From 'how do you actually hold a brush properly' to 'what is paint and how do I actually mix that stuff?' The starting point is to learn with pleasure. Drawing and painting from observation - basis from 16 years with Gurt Swanenberg Want to start drawing and painting? Or do you want to further develop your skills? In this basic course you will learn to develop your own handwriting based on various studies into perception. In the lessons you work on assignments within a specific theme. Within each theme offered, a technical skill is presented, and you learn about how artists work with this. Within the theme, the emphasis can be on color, composition, perspective or another visual concept. The most important thing is discovering the possibilities to create an image, and the pleasure and satisfaction that gives. We discuss the work in class and individually so that you become aware of your own handwriting, strengths and weaknesses and how others experience your work. That can be confrontational, but also extremely educational. You also learn from each other because you work together on the same assignment. What could such a theme look like? In various object studies based on objects displayed in the studio, we simplify them into pure geometric shapes. In black-and-white studies, for example, we work based on the work of artists associated with the “Die Neuen Sachlichkeit” movement. For example, you will get to know the photography of Karl Blossfeld or the still life paintings of Alexander Kanoldt. But we also look at drawings by Max Beckmann to study his compositions. In a form-residual study we then look, for example, at the work of Giorgio Morandi to study concepts such as repoussoir and cut-off. By looking at the work of others, you learn to develop your own preferences and to argue for these in conversations with your teacher and fellow students. What are you taking with you? All necessary materials and tools are arranged by us, except for special requests. So you don't have to bring anything from home. Material costs are not included in the course price. name: Tekenen & schilderen – vervolg vanaf 16 jaar
description_short: To paint? Everything is possible! Drawing and painting can be done in many ways. In this course with 2.5 hour lessons, each teacher has their own approach.
description_full: Drawing & painting – continued from 16 years Back to overview Painting? Everything is possible! Drawing and painting can be done in many ways. In this course with 2.5 hour lessons, each teacher has their own approach. Attention to the subject and the way you can portray it, painting in your own personal way, trying out different techniques, or deepening them. Painting pleasure and challenge are paramount. With this course you are assured of quality: VAK teachers are all professionally trained, so they understand their profession as artists and as teacher-supervisors! Read more about the specialisms in the description of the teacher. Painting for everyone! Beginner or advanced, for everyone from 16 to 101 there are plenty of opportunities in the course to improve your painting level. We recommend that real starters first take the beginners course. Register Teachers Mariska van den Enden Niels Janssen Jan Wisse Wilma Keizer Victor Roerade Machiel van Soest What will you learn in the drawing & painting course? In this course you will learn how to choose your subjects, how to start imagining your subject and how to develop it further. The teacher introduces themes or topics for this purpose. You will learn about composition, color and working in different techniques. Each teacher has their own specialties and preferences. Through personal guidance, attention is paid to your own way of working or its development. Your development with painting and your painting pleasure are central. Teacher Machiel van Soest Machiel van Soest's lessons invite you to develop your own visual language and find your own working method. There is plenty of room to experiment with different techniques, materials and surfaces. In a creative and pleasant atmosphere you gain experience that you can draw on for your later work. The themes on the program offer unexpected perspectives on common subjects such as still life, landscape and portrait and vary from realism to abstract. During the lesson we will gradually delve deeper into the visual elements that make up a painting, such as composition, shape and residual form, color scheme and contrast effect. By means of a short presentation in advance, Machiel van Soest provides each new theme with an art historical context with many inspiring examples that encourage you to explore new territory. At the end of each lesson there is a group discussion. Teacher Niels Janssen The basis of this course is your own creativity and how you can express it in drawings and paintings. By responding to the assignments, you go through the entire process from ideation to the end result for every work you create. This is done in consultation with Niels Janssen. Gradually all aspects of drawing and painting are discussed. Color, composition, different materials and techniques, form and residual form, abstraction and figuration, the types of contrasts you can use, and so on. But the core question always remains: How do you make your own dream world visible in drawings and paintings? So that upon completion you can say: That work is mine and no one else's! The lessons are in groups and in an atmosphere of trust. We work hard, but don't forget to laugh and have a good time. Niels Janssen has been teaching at various institutions for art education in the region since 1998 and is therefore a very experienced teacher. He regularly exhibits at galleries in The Hague, Rotterdam and Amsterdam. Niels is convinced that everyone carries with them their own world of ideas and representations. Through assignments he challenges you to make that invisible world visible. But as Willem Elsschot already wrote: “There are laws and practical objections that stand in the way between dream and action.” Niels will help you with great enthusiasm and humor to create your dream drawing or painting...

name: Vrij schilderen vanaf 18 jaar
description_short: Let yourself be guided by the painting, learn to see what is happening on the canvas and be amazed by what was not there before. Experience the freedom!
description_full: Free painting from the age of 18 Back to the overview Free painting? Experiment, discover your own visual language and develop your own signature! Abstract, figurative or realistic? Is there a difference? Actually not, the same principles apply to every work of art, whether abstract, realistic or figurative. For example, to create a realistic work one must learn to look 'abstractly', to look at the subject 'meaninglessly' and translate this into lines, surfaces, proportions and shades of light and color. These are the 'building blocks' of every painting. This course shows that abstract and figurative go hand in hand. A figurative painting always has abstract elements and an abstract painting always has a connection with reality. From observation, fantasy or from the material, whatever starting point you choose, if you are aware of the building blocks you will gain control over the painting process. The right structure and technique gives you control over the paint. And therein lies freedom, you can do whatever you want! If you want to deviate from a similarity that is too compelling, then you have come to the right place. This course is suitable for both figurative and abstract painters. We use these sources of inspiration in the course to become familiar with the visual elements and the structure of a painting or drawing. The 'problems' to be solved, such as the drawing, light/dark distribution and color, are always systematically discussed based on these five themes. name: Flamenco – intermediate (live muziek) vanaf 18 jaar
description_short: Flamenco is sultry, strict, challenging and explosive. You go along with the rhythm and throw yourself passionately into this exciting and intense dance form, with controlled temperament and stylized passion.
description_full: Flamenco – intermediate (live music) from 18 years Back to the overview Are you going for rhythmic footwork, graceful arms and proud looks? Then this is your course. Flamenco is sultry, strict, challenging and explosive. You go along with the rhythm and throw yourself passionately into this exciting and intense dance form, with a controlled temperament and stylized passion. Flamenco dancing is not limited by age. In Spain, flamenco is taught at a young age, but that does not mean that you cannot learn it, young or older, that does not matter either. The advantage of flamenco dancing is that you do not need a partner to dance with you. With a few exceptions, namely the Sevillanas, but then you dance together. Flamenco dancing is not just for the ladies, the gentlemen are also welcome! Register Teachers Everdine de Vreede What do you learn? You start with a good foundation, often with the dance de Sevillanas. This dance is a festive folk dance that is integrated into flamenco. The Sevillanas consists of 4 coplas (couplets) and has a fixed structure. You will learn, among other things, coordination between footwork and arms, learning to listen to the music, palmas (rhythmic hand clapping), contra tiempo (clapping against the basic rhythm). Performance We usually work towards a performance or a proposal. This does not mean that you are obliged to participate, but experience shows that everyone is on stage with full conviction and great pleasure at the end of the dance season! Study trip to Seville Teacher Everdine de Vreede organizes a study trip to Seville once a year. She has been doing this with great pleasure for ten years to introduce students to the flamenco atmosphere. You actually live there for a week, because you don't stay in a hotel, but in an apartment, alone or with your fellow students, somewhere near the school. This way you experience and experience the atmosphere of living among the Sevillanos. You will go to the flamenco school Taller Flamenco where you can take dance lessons, in class as well as privately. Or you want to improve your Spanish language and take conversation lessons. Take a look at the website www.tallerflamenco.com to see which other classes you could take during that week. This study trip is only intended for the students, so no partners are accompanying you. The costs of the study trip are not included in the course fee for the dance class. Useful to know It is important that you wear sturdy shoes with a sturdy heel of a maximum of 5 cm high and not shoes with a black sole, as this could damage the dance floor. It is not necessary to purchase flamenco shoes immediately. In terms of clothing, it is advisable to wear cotton clothing, which absorbs moisture well. A long skirt or pants, as long as it is comfortable. Lesson format Group lesson with live music accompanied by a flamenco guitarist and a percussionist. description_full: Flamenco – intermediate (live music) from 18 years Back to the overview Go deeper into the world of Flamenco Are you going for more rhythmic footwork, hand clapping, graceful arms and proud looks? And you have at least 1 year of experience with flamenco dancing? Then this is the course for you. Flamenco is sultry and strict, challenging and explosive. Get into the rhythm and immerse yourself with passion in this exciting and intense dance form, with controlled temperament and stylized passion. Learn several basic techniques of Flamenco dance and register today for this follow-up course in Flamenco dance lessons. This course consists of 34 lessons. Each lesson lasts one hour. And is given on Monday evenings from 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Flamenco intermediate (live music) 18+ This Flamenco dance course is for young and old with at least 1 year of experience. After this course you can possibly move on to the advanced. It is a course for the Spain enthusiast. Learn to be present at parties in Spain, especially with the Sevillanas dance. Both men and women can dance Flamenco. Register Teachers Wil Lambregts What will you learn during the intermediate Flamenco dance course? In these 34 lessons, each one hour long (with live guitar accompaniment), the following topics are discussed to form a good basis for dancing Flamenco in various palos (styles): Foot technique Foot technique ultimately results in a rhythmic warm-up for the leg and foot muscles. Alegrías Rumba Track Previously learned techniques and styles are tracked. Playing castanets If there is enough interest, learn to play the castanets. Flamenco Tangos Alegrias A cheerful, pure Flamenco dance that focuses on consistency, sense of rhythm and melody, but also on the total presentation (skirt, arm and hand movements). Sevillanas A festive folk dance that is integrated into Flamenco dance. This dance is popular throughout Spain and is danced at all kinds of occasions such as weddings, parties and ferias (even in the disco). This dance involves techniques that are important for dancing other forms of Flamenco. Dancing to live music During the lessons, live music is played so that you are musically guided. If you dance faster or slower, the guidance will follow suit. When dancing to a CD there is a fixed beat and melody. The melody can also be different every time in live guitar music, but it is always in the palo (style) in which you dance. This course is also good for general dance training. What do I take with me? For the Flamenco dance intermediate course, shoes with a block heel and casual clothing are sufficient for the time being. You also need castanets. In some cases, castanets can also be loaned out. It is not necessary to have castanets during the trial lesson. Possible purchase can be made via the teacher. The teacher teaches you to find the right balance, pays attention to your posture and helps where necessary. And what about the appearance during the dance? We are working on that too! The costs of this study trip are not included in this beginners course. Good to know It is a group lesson, but there is certainly room for individual attention from your teacher. Dancing at the barre, au milieu and through the hall you will soon feel like a real ballet dancer. Sign up for a trial lesson! description_full: Classical ballet & modern dance 10-12 years Back to overview Become a real theater dancer with classical ballet and modern dance in one lesson! A solid dance lesson in which a lot of attention is paid to developing and improving your dance technique. Do you want that? Then come to the Classical ballet & modern dance course for 10-12 years. In this lesson we work on (deepening) the dance technique of classical ballet and modern dance. Classical ballet is an elegant dance style that provides an excellent foundation for any dancer. Modern dance is an expressive dance style that is based on natural movements such as jumping, turning, waving, falling and rolling. In class we also pay attention to performing choreographies and creating pieces with, for example, a story or theme. Register Teachers Katelijn Lindeijer What do you learn? You learn the technique associated with classical ballet and modern dance. You dance classical and modern repertoire and choreographies. You learn to dance and create together. You dance for an audience at least once a year in a performance or presentation. Of course, fun is central! About the lessons The lesson is always in groups. During the lesson everyone dances together, as a duo or trio and at times you are allowed to dance alone. The teacher pays attention to every student and will also encourage each student individually to develop his or her talents. Entry and progression After this course you can progress to, for example, Classical ballet and choreo 12+, Modern Jazz 12 - 18 years or you can audition for the selection class Classical and modern 10 - 12 years. description_full: Classical ballet and choreo 12-17 years Back to the overview Dancing like in real classical ballets such as 'Swan Lake' or 'The Nutcracker'? Do you also want to learn to dance beautiful pirouettes or do you want to become better at classical ballet technique? Register now for the Classical ballet and choreo 12+ class. In these ballet lessons you will take your ballet technique and dancing pleasure to a higher level. In addition to technique, you also learn to develop your artistry and musicality. We also work on learning pieces of ballet repertoire and also pay attention to creating choreography yourself. Register Teachers Katelijn Lindeijer What do you learn during the dance class? In these ballet lessons you will work on good posture, flexibility, coordination, balance and train for stronger muscles and feet. You feel strong and graceful at the same time and learn the movements as they are performed in the Vaganova technique and Royal Academy of Dancing. The exercises at the barre prepare your body for the center (au Milieu) where twists and jumps are also done. We work on pieces of ballet repertoire (fixed choreographies) and also learn to make our own choreographies through various assignments. You dance once a year in a presentation or performance in costume that fits the classical or modern ballet tradition. An important component is the music. You dance and learn to listen to the music. All lessons are aimed at discovering and increasing pleasure in dance! During the lesson we all dance together, as a duo or trio and at times you are allowed to dance alone. The teacher pays attention to every student and will also encourage each student individually to develop his or her talents. Enrollment during the year is almost always possible! name: Moderne dans – advanced vanaf 18 jaar
description_short: This musical modern lesson from Sanne is based on the Limón technique: with attention to breath, flow, gravity and organic movement.
description_full: Modern dance – advanced from 18 years Back to the overview Enjoy moving to inspiring music! Modern dance is earthy, dynamic and has much freer movements than classical ballet. This musical modern lesson from Sanne is based on the Limón technique: with attention to breath, flow, gravity and organic movement. Guaranteed wonderful exercise and you will notice that it is not just a physical challenge: you learn to coordinate, work musically, use your imagination and increase your spatial insight, so you also train your brain! 'Dancing is like taking a mini vacation from the stress of everyday - you have to be in the moment.' - Ofelia de la Valette Modern dance Advanced for adults You have been dancing in one of the academic techniques for at least 10 years and you want to challenge yourself further when it comes to your dance technique, your ability to move great, your musicality and your coordination. Because there are many differences between modern dance techniques, styles and teachers: take a trial lesson to see whether this lesson suits you and whether you suit this lesson! Register Teachers Sanne van der Put What will you learn during these modern dance lessons? The lessons start with a gentle warm-up and progress through more energetic dance combinations across the floor to a dancing choreographic combination. You conclude with a short cool down, often with various stretches. In this way you work freely on many aspects of body and mind: think of coordination, strength and flexibility, articulated movement, consciously using your breath in your body and spatial and dancing movement. You not only feel physically fitter if you dance often, but also mentally. In addition, you will experience a better posture in your daily life because you become much more aware of what your body can do. About the lessons You will be in a group of a maximum of 16 students. We usually work on technique, enjoyment of dance and regularly on choreography pieces. If the opportunity arises, it is possible to participate in presentations, performances and events - this is always optional. What do I take with me? During classes, wear comfortable clothing (sports, dance or yoga clothing) that does not hinder your movement and leave jewelry at home as much as possible. We dance in socks or bare feet, whichever you prefer. Please bring a warm top with you in case it is a bit chillier in the studio or in the hallways. There is a changing room, but do not leave valuables there. description_short: Do you want to dance more than once a week, work extra on your dance technique and learn more about choreographing? Then dance along with Selection and choreography.
description_full: Selection & choreography 12 to 18 years Back to the overview Do you want to dance more than once a week, work extra on your dance technique and learn more about choreography? Are you already taking dance lessons at De VAK and would you like to take a second lesson? Then dance along with Selection and choreography for 13 to 18 years. In this lesson you will delve deeper into the techniques of modern and jazz styles. In blocks you work on the correct dance technique, empathy, musicality, strength and flexibility that comes with modern or jazz. In addition, in this group we work together on cool choreographies and you learn how to create a beautiful dance yourself and in a group. We will also perform some of these dances during dance competitions or a performance. The selection class lessons are for dancers who can do just that little bit more, but above all want to do a little more. Having a passion for extra dancing is the first admission requirement. Together with the dance teacher of your 'regular' dance class, you will look and decide whether you are suitable for training in this group in order to become an even better dancer. This lesson is a group lesson. During the lesson, the teacher gives a lot of personal attention to create a pleasant atmosphere and allow each student to further develop at their own level. Register Teachers Celine Braakman What will you learn during this lesson? In this lesson you will delve deeper into the techniques of modern and jazz. You improve your memorization of steps, learn to present yourself and work on a beautiful dance posture. You will learn more about choreographing and the process that goes with it. In this lesson, fun is paramount, but there will be slightly higher demands on concentration and focus. What do you wear during class? Well-fitting leggings (preferably black) and a black training top, t-shirt or leotard. In consultation with the students, the teacher decides whether the group will participate in a dance competition. This may involve an additional contribution. description_full: Dare to Close! from 18 years Back to the overview Writing a good poem: difficult or scary? No, it's a matter of courage and action. This course quickly removes the difficult and scary aspects. It might be a bit exciting to see what you dared to write again and what your fellow students think about it. Enjoying writing and creativity are paramount. And you also learn a lot: that there are different sources of inspiration; that there are more means than just rhyme to turn a text into a poem; that there are many ways to start a poem. That there are all kinds of poems for various occasions: striking, sweet, crazy, comforting, humorous, moving, etc. In short: poetry = dare = just do it! At home you complete the poem in your own time and pace. You take the poem with you to the next lesson and we will discuss the results together. You receive and give constructive feedback. description_short: Are you looking for an inspiring writing course? Explore different styles and genres: column, fairy tale, the Very Short Story, poem.
description_full: Ink and inspiration – writing with pleasure from the age of 18 Back to the overview Creative writing – basic with bonus Can't seem to get around to it? Do the stories stay in your head? Or do you start writing but stop after the third paragraph? Then read on. In the basic creative writing course you can write anything you want. You experience that there are different ways to tell your story. Sometimes the shape is very tight, sometimes not. One time you write a poem, the next time a flaming column and after that perhaps a false fairy tale. Surprise yourself! The writing teacher will give you an inspiring perspective every time, so you will surprise yourself and learn writing techniques at the same time. This way your texts become more and more convincing. Good luck while you write! During the lessons, your creative process comes first. You will have time to come up with your stories, including through appealing example texts and association assignments. You tumble through your head and find starting points for your text: poetic patterns, intriguing impressions, frisky dialogues. The writing techniques are explained and practiced step by step. That is why this course is suitable for everyone, experienced or not. Register Teachers Marieke van der Honing Sounds good, right? Keep reading, because there's more! Writing in a group has great advantages. You will notice how many variations arise from one assignment. You learn a lot from that. And you will receive feedback on your texts from the teacher and your fellow students. You won't get that close to your readers easily! name: Tai Chi – basis vanaf 16 jaar
description_short: Discover your body, clear your head and find balance with Tai Chi.Tai Chi Basics: for anyone who wants to stand more firmly on the earth.
description_full: Tai Chi – basics from 16 years Back to the overview Discover your body, clear your head and find balance with Tai Chi Tai Chi is an ancient Chinese movement art that promotes your vitality, increases your resistance and makes you more aware and balanced in life. During the lessons you will learn to walk a Tai Chi form, slowly and in a fixed order. You will receive individual instructions to move as relaxed as possible, so that energy can flow freely through your body. Tai Chi Basics: for everyone who wants to stand more firmly on the earth Do you want to live life with attention? Becoming aware of 'self-evident things' such as walking and thinking? And thus further discover your (inner) life? Register now for this basic Tai Chi course! Tai Chi is suitable for all ages, young to old. Moreover, Tai Chi is also suitable for people with a chronic condition, people who are recovering from a long-term illness, or people who have complaints of stress or burnout. Register Teachers Lely Oei Discover your body, let go of your thoughts and experience peace! In this beginners course you will learn the basics of Tai Chi. The basic principles of Tai Chi are learned using the 24-Yang style. Standing like a tree, consciously walking 'Tai Chi', and building up your posture. In slowness, you become aware of your posture and way of moving. When posture, slowness, and movement coincide, you can start to feel the Qi (life energy). Equally important is learning to observe and let go of thoughts and emotions (from the past). Natural deep breathing can help with this. All these aspects provide deep relaxation. Lely guides you with knowledge of and respect for the ancient Chinese sources, translated into your daily life. By practicing Tai Chi you literally become more confident and from there you can face the world with more confidence. About the lessons The composition of the group is diverse. Lely Oei is used to serving different levels in 1 lesson. Usually the basic course is followed a few times before you move on to the advanced course. What are you wearing? What are you wearing? It is important for this course to be able to get moving. Therefore, wear clothes that you can move comfortably in, and indoor shoes with a flexible sole. These can be sneakers, ballet shoes, or socks with studs. A bottle of water against thirst is always nice. If we train outside, which we do in nice weather, make sure you stay warm. description_full: Tai Chi – in-depth from 16 years Back to the overview Immerse yourself in Tai Chi and really get to know yourself Are you familiar with Tai Chi and do you really want to connect with yourself and your environment with the help of Tai Chi? Then this course is for you. The way Lely teaches Tai Chi, you learn everything about yourself, your body, your thinking and your feelings. You increase your resistance and get more energy. And at the same time, Tai Chi teaches you to connect with others. Lely teaches Tai Chi with knowledge of ancient sources, translated into our contemporary world. The Yang style is central to the lessons. You will receive individual instructions on a physical and mental level. This way you learn to move in a relaxed manner, so that energy can flow freely through your body. Register Teachers Lely Oei Tai Chi In-depth: for anyone who is looking for more balance in their life Have you followed the beginners course (a few times)? Have you practiced Tai Chi in the past? Or do you want more depth in your practice and insight into the origins of the Tai Chi movements? Register now for this Tai Chi course! If you are unsure which course suits you, please contact us for a trial lesson. The 24 yang style is generally assumed to be known. Peace in your mind, relaxed in your body, steady in your shoes. In this course you will further develop the skills you have previously acquired. From learning through concentration, you learn from attention. This will teach you to relax even more, allow your Qi to flow more easily, allow you to go into depth more quickly and get into a flow more quickly. Tai Chi gives you peace of mind, insight into your body, better fitness and more life energy. You become aware of how you move in daily life and how you can break ingrained and (un)healthy patterns. This way you learn to move relaxed in a healthy, future-proof way. You get to know your body, thoughts and emotions. And then let go so that you experience more space and freedom. This will make your Qi, life energy, flow better. You will also receive tools to continue working on this at home, without guidance. In this way you learn to perform the form independently and you are able to integrate the wisdom of Tai Chi into your life. You will have a more stable and positive outlook on life. But above all, it is fun and relaxing to do! We refine the 24-Yang style, and learn a new form. You learn to perform the 24 form independently in your own environment. This allows you to practice Tai Chi whenever you feel like it. You will also experience that you can multiply the Qi even further in a group. We mainly learn the Yang style and the basic principles of standing exercises, such as 'standing like a tree', are further developed. You are not only able to perform the exercises in class under supervision, but you can also do them independently in your own environment. This allows you to practice Tai Chi whenever you feel like it or when you need Tai Chi. You will also experience that when practicing Tai Chi in a group you can multiply the Qi even further. description_full: Antillean music from 18 years old Back to the overview Discover and play music with a nod to sultry dances and refined melodies from the Antillean islands. In this new course you will play Antillean classical and traditional music from the Caribbean part of our kingdom, a music style that is not well known in the Netherlands. This music style has European, African and South American roots. You will learn to play different rhythms such as the Antillean waltz, the dansa, the mazurka and the tumba. We play compositions by Curaçaoan and Aruban composers, such as Rudolph Th. Palm, Cornelis Boskaljon, Jacobo Conrad, Rufo Wever and popular songs by Rudy Plaate and Padú Lampe. If you want to discover and play Antillean classical and traditional music, then you have come to the right place with this course. The pieces are mostly instrumental. There are also songs sung in Papiamentu. For whom? If you already play classical music, folk music or dance music and want to learn to play a new style of music, then this course is for you. Even if you already know the style and would like to play it yourself in an ensemble, you are welcome. Mastering your instrument and being able to read notes is a requirement. Singers are also welcome. Register Teachers Randy Winterdal What are we going to do? We make music together in an ensemble. Teamwork is important; attention is paid to this in class. Every instrument fulfills a role. The leading party and the supporting party complement the whole. You learn to listen to each other and respond to each other. What should I bring? If you play the violin, flute, guitar, cuatro or bass guitar, please bring your own instrument. There is a piano. There are also percussion instruments, vocal equipment and amplifiers available. Parties are taken care of. description_short: Join our bassoon ensemble and experience the fun of playing together! Learn to play in a group with other bassoonists – a unique experience! description_full: Bassoon ensemble from 18 years Back to overview Play in our bassoon ensemble and experience the fun of playing together! Learn to play in a group with other bassoonists – a unique experience! As a bassoon teacher, orchestra leader and workshop organizer, I strongly believe that making music together is one of the best ways to develop your musical skills. By playing with others you not only work on expressiveness and ear training, but you also create unique musical experiences. In this bassoon ensemble you will learn how to play together as a group, listen to each other and create a rich sound together. An inspiring opportunity to take your game to the next level. The Bassoon Ensemble is for adults of all levels who want to be part of a unique ensemble and learn more by playing together! This course is intended for adults aged 18 and over, regardless of their experience playing together or their level on the bassoon. Whether you are a beginner or advanced, there is room for everyone to grow. An ensemble is a great place to further develop your skills, with a diverse group of bassoonists. Whether you play the bass line or the more complex melodies, you always find your place in the ensemble and can further develop your musical talent. Register Teachers Maria Selvas Bou In this course you will play repertoire in different styles, from classical works to modern music, within a bassoon ensemble. We not only develop your bassoon skills, but also other musical skills, such as ear training, improvisation and playing without sheet music. We also help you to think creatively and work better together in a group, which is important for you as a musician and as a bassoonist. The course consists of group lessons that take place every two weeks. Each lesson starts with a warm-up, followed by playing repertoire in different styles. We end the lesson with a fun activity that stimulates your creativity and collaboration. During the year we work together towards a final concert, where we can present what we have learned and share a special musical experience together. Good to know Students only need to bring their own instrument. If you have specific music you want to play, feel free to bring it along! description_short: Free Academy Bigband plays pieces with great enthusiasm and energy that range from sultry jazz to swinging funk.
description_full: Free Academy Big Band from 16 years Back to the overview Free Academy Big Band consists of eighteen musicians from 18 years and older, in all age groups. They play pieces with great enthusiasm and energy that range from sultry jazz to swinging funk. The company wants to rapidly improve the quality of its playing. To be able to play in the Free Academy Big Band, you must have had several years of lessons and preferably also some experience playing together, for example in smaller groups. It's nice if you can read the page quickly. Of course you have to enjoy playing swinging music. The rhythm section is basically complete. There is room for a new bass guitarist. There is also certainly room for brass: trumpets and a few trombones. Do you want to play along? In that case, prior consultation with the conductor is necessary. It is possible to attend 2 to 3 rehearsals on a trial basis. Register Teachers Fenna Volmer What does an evening with the Free Academy Big Band look like? During an evening we like to rehearse about four to six songs per evening. There is little time to instruct groups separately. A new piece must sound reasonably good from the start and we then put the finishing touches on it during rehearsals. There is room for solos in almost every piece. Playing solos is not mandatory, especially in the beginning. There is plenty of room and understanding if you want to give it a try. And sometimes we also have a drink afterwards, for fun. There is no bar in the room, so we bring our own. Performance The Free Academy Big Band performs several times a year. This can be both indoors and outdoors, for example at a festival, in a jazz cafe, in a restaurant with a large garden, on an evening of lights in Delft or at a party in a hall, etc. Useful to know As a member/participant of the FABB you play your own instrument. We rehearse in Rijswijk, in a former scouting building. The VAK provides music stands, percussion and amplifiers. As for clothing: sometimes we agree with each other in which colors we perform, for example black with a red accent. That depends a bit on the location where we perform. description_full: Jazz ensemble 'Jazz & Beyond' from 18 years Back to overview Jazz is an adventure, experience it! The jazz ensemble Jazz & Beyond uses a broad repertoire: bebop, hard bop, mainstream, modern jazz, Latin jazz and other related styles. Pieces by Thelonious Monk, Miles Davis, Wayne Shorter, Herbie Hancock, but also by Paquito d' Rivera or Dexter Gordon and many others are included. In the weekly lessons/meetings, attention is paid to ensemble playing, dynamics, improvisation, chord theory, scales, etc. The group performs regularly, both inside and outside De VAK. If you are interested and have some experience with improvisation, come along and experience the magic of playing and improvising together! Jazz ensemble for advanced students 18+ Jazz ensemble Jazz & Beyond is for adults with a broad interest in jazz music. You have a reasonable command of instruments and reading notes is not a problem. The ensemble is for advanced students. Register Teachers Ed Baatsen What do you learn from jazz & beyond? During the meetings of the jazz ensemble, a lot of attention is paid to the following matters: ensemble playing, timing, solo structure, theory, such as scales and chord theory, dynamics, interaction, analysis of pieces, etc. When you play in a band you also learn to listen to others, to accept and to work together. Jazz & Beyond is an instrumental ensemble, without singing, and plays a very diverse repertoire in addition to jazz standards. Let's say: jazz from 1945 to the present…. About the lessons The jazz ensemble course consists of 36 lessons, 1 hour per week. The repertoire now consists of more than 100 (!) pieces. During the year we often work towards a performance. description_full: Music on Lap (Toddler) 1 to 2 years Back to the overview How much fun is it to make music together with your toddler? You don't have to be musical. description_short: Recent hits and evergreens in an original polyphonic guise. Come sing along with Popkoor From The Top!
description_full: Pop choir – From the Top from 16 years Back to the overview Recent hits and evergreens in an original polyphonic style Do you like singing and are you looking for a fun group to make music with? Come sing along with Popkoor From The Top! From The Top is a relatively small choir with a focus on the pleasure of singing, which of course requires attention to singing technique, breathing and interpretation. We usually sing in three parts and work towards fun performance moments. In terms of repertoire, you can count on pop music from the 1950s to the present: from the Beach Boys via Simon & Garfunkel and Cyndi Lauper to Adele, Coldplay and Ed Sheeran, for example. If that sounds like something to you, then read on. Singing is healthy and fun. From the age of 16 you are welcome at From The Top. Your background, education or musical knowledge is not that important in this choir. Your enthusiasm for singing is! Or as jazz legend Ella Fitzgerald said: 'The only thing better than singing is more singing!' Register Teachers Mariska Simon What do you learn from singing in a choir? After singing in a choir for a while, you learn to trust your own voice. You learn how to collaborate, how sheet music works (without necessarily reading notes) and you get to know a lot of new people. We work with arrangements of different levels. So that it doesn't get boring. Attention is paid to voice and breath. Singing in a choir is quite exciting at first, but you will notice that you can do more than you think! What should I bring? The teacher brings sheet music and lyrics. There is also a Google Drive with sing-along versions of the parties. Bring your own folder where you can keep the songs. A pencil or pen is always handy. Wear comfortable clothes and shoes. Singing on pumps is quite a challenge. description_short: Do you want to learn to use your own voice and do you like singing in a group?
description_full: Voice formation for beginners and advanced students from 21 years old Back to the overview Do you want to learn to use your own voice and do you like singing in a group? Can you already keep tone, but do you want to learn more about the technique of singing and practice with it? Do you want to learn how to get more out of your voice or are you encountering certain problems? Are you less of a soloist but do you enjoy singing in a group and do you find it a challenge to learn simple yet polyphonic arrangements with some guidance? All these facets are discussed during the course 'Voice formation for advanced students'. Voice training for adults For people who can maintain tone but who would like to have more insight into and control over their (singing) voice in combination with the pleasure of singing in a group. Who like to use tools to work with polyphonic arrangements, performance and singing with feeling. Are you unsure whether the level of these lessons suits you? Take a trial lesson where both you and the teacher can determine whether the course suits you. Register Teachers Hannah Ybeles Smit What will you learn during the Voice Formation course? The first part of the lesson is spent on singing technique with the help of explanations and exercises. You learn to know and prepare your own range. You will learn about relaxation, breathing, breath support, how to sing low and high notes. You will learn the difference between chest and head voice and attention will be paid to techniques such as EVT and C VT. The second part of the lesson is spent on choral singing, building up a polyphonic repertoire and also working on expression, rhythm, performance and for those who want: solo singing. What should I bring? Voice shaping works with Dropbox. You will receive a link by email with which you can access the folder. Here you will find song lyrics, sometimes sheet music and sung parts with which you can practice. During class it is necessary to bring a pen and a folder in which you can put printed texts (yourself).
